Definition: Percentage of total electricity generation from renewable sources (hydro, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass). Indicates energy sustainability and potential for distributed power solutions relevant to ICT infrastructure in off-grid areas.
revision_notes: Fetched the cited Statista page: it reports the share of renewable energy in installed generation capacity (2023), a different metric from this variable's definition (share of actual generation), so it does not directly evidence the score even though the resulting code happened to be correct. Ran fresh searches and found consistent generation-share data: countryeconomy.com (IRENA/EIA-based) shows renewable electricity generation at 3.06% in 2022, 3.94% in 2023 and 4.40% in 2024; African Manager, citing Tunisia's Energy Research Unit, reports the renewable generation share slipped to 4.03% in 2025 (from 4.4% in 2024) as fossil fuels held roughly 96% of the mix despite an 11% jump in installed renewable capacity to 1.21 GW. Both sources were fetched and read in full. This confirms Value Code 1 (<10%) is correct on the generation-share scale; the original comment mixed up capacity and generation shares but did not change the outcome.
revised_comments: Renewable sources, chiefly wind and solar with negligible hydropower, account for approximately 4% of Tunisia's electricity generation (4.03% in 2025, down slightly from 4.40% in 2024), according to Energy Research Unit data reported by African Manager and consistent with generation-share estimates for 2022-2024. Natural gas dominates the generation mix at roughly 95-96%. Installed renewable capacity has expanded faster than output, reaching around 1.21 GW by the end of 2025 (mostly solar), but this has not yet translated into a proportionate rise in the share of generation, which remains well below 10%.
